name: Farren's Proof
summary: In Southshore, Marshal Redpath sends Lieutenant Farren Orinelle orders to turn toward the naga on the Eastern Strand. He wants Orinelle to drive them back and report in person.

sections.title: A Shift in Command
sections.body: Marshal Redpath sends word across Southshore to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Reports tell of naga incursions on the Eastern Strand, and Redpath wants Orinelle focused on that threat. The lieutenant must set aside other concerns, drive back the naga, and report his progress to the Marshal in person.

sections.title: Rivalry on the Coast
sections.body: Lieutenant Farren Orinelle suspects Marshal Redpath wants credit for calming the Eastern Strand. He thinks Redpath is using intelligence they both received to claim the garrison's work. Unwilling to let his commander earn a promotion through his soldiers' labor, Orinelle begins devising another way to win favor with the crown.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this delivery?
faq.answer: Marshal Redpath's orders direct Lieutenant Farren Orinelle to face the naga on Hillsbrad's Eastern Strand and report his progress to the Marshal in person.

faq.q: Why does Farren Orinelle react bitterly to Redpath's orders?
faq.answer: Orinelle believes Redpath is acting on the same military intelligence they both received. He fears the Marshal means to claim credit for clearing the coast and gain a promotion through Orinelle's hard work.

faq.q: Where is the Eastern Strand located?
faq.answer: The Eastern Strand runs along the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills, southeast of Southshore. Naga have made encampments on its sand.

faq.q: What comes next after delivering this message?
faq.answer: After the delivery, Orinelle devises his own scheme instead of simply following Redpath's authority. His plan sends couriers down the coast toward high command in 'Stormwind Ho!'.

faq.q: Who are the leaders involved in this exchange?
faq.answer: Marshal Redpath commands Southshore's garrison, and Lieutenant Farren Orinelle serves under him as a field lieutenant overseeing coastal defense.

faq.q: Does this assignment require any combat?
faq.answer: No. The delivery is an exchange between officers in Southshore, though it concerns the military response to naga along the shore.

angles.text: The exchange reveals rivalries over rank and recognition within Southshore's garrison, even as the northern outpost faces threats.
As an Alliance warrior, you may recognize the strain between proving yourself in battle and navigating officers' ambitions.
